input_authorities.input: Windows-first single-user companion runtime; companion-add-in communication disabled until G-ADDIN and ADR-010
Office add-in manifest permissions and requirement sets remain feature-scoped and disabled
pairing-root.dpapi reservation, DPAPI blob rules, and memory-only session-secret boundary
EWS-to-REST conversion, displayMessageFormAsync gating, webLink validation, and the random non-secret review-link handle rule
review_link_boundary payload, prohibited list, and deferred activation to ADR-010 and G-ADDIN
exact record fields, retention, and prohibited content; PRIV-XREC-010 pairing/session secret exclusion

transport_boundary.preferred_internal_transport: named pipes for companion-internal and native-UI traffic
transport_boundary.addin_candidate_transport: a same-user loopback web bridge is the sole candidate transport for the Office add-in, used only if the runnable packaged G-ADDIN spike proves asset hosting, certificate/network, discovery, and bootstrap boundaries on every advertised client
prohibited_assumptions: a named pipe is reachable from Office.js
Graph delegated scopes authorize add-in operations

bootstrap_boundary.race_defense: two concurrent first-pair attempts on the same port resolve to at most one bound pairing; the loser observes a fail-closed rejection rather than a second silent binding
bootstrap_boundary.replay_defense: a replayed nonce is rejected once its single use is consumed or its expiry passes
bootstrap_boundary.brute_force_defense: pairing verification is rate- and attempt-bounded so brute-forcing the verification value fails closed rather than degrading into an open window
bootstrap_boundary.unpaired_command_rule: no unpaired command exists; every command requires a bound, live session, so a malicious local page issuing loopback requests before pairing completes is rejected

session_boundary.authority: least-authority command-scoped in-memory sessions authorizing only the specific companion commands the add-in surface requires: review, evidence navigation, settings, and status
session_boundary.persistence: every session secret is held in memory only and is never written to the database, a DPAPI blob, disk, or a log
session_boundary.rotation: a session rotates on reconnect and is revoked on account change
session_boundary.stale_rule: a session bound to a prior account or a stale companion generation is rejected, not silently reused
session_boundary.residual_limitation: this is a same-user boundary only; it defends against a malicious local web page or a different local account, not against code already running as the same authenticated OS user

network_boundary.host_origin_validation: exact Host and Origin values are validated against a closed allowlist
network_boundary.csrf_defense: an explicit CSRF defense independent of cookies is required
network_boundary.binding: loopback addresses only; no LAN, wildcard, or 0.0.0.0 bind
network_boundary.rate_and_size_limits: request rate and size limits are enforced
network_boundary.dns_rebinding: hostnames that resolve to a loopback address after the fact from an external-looking origin are rejected

prohibited: a general-purpose trusted root with a retained signing key
certificate_boundary.scope_if_selected: current-user only, limited to the exact tested loopback names, using a non-exportable private key ACL'd to the user and application
certificate_boundary.lifecycle: explicit issue, rotation, expiry, and replacement behavior
certificate_boundary.cleanup: completely removed on disconnect and uninstall; failure of any trust cleanup step or client path blocks the add-in

review_link_boundary.payload: one random, non-secret, opaque loop handle and no authority, exactly the ADR-009 payload
review_link_boundary.activation: an authenticated, per-user, account-bound resolution of that handle against the current loop state
review_link_boundary.unsupported_client_behavior: omit the link or show a fixed safe-fallback instruction; never fall back to embedding authority in the link

content_boundary.scope: applies to every add-in surface, not only the review link

native_fallback_boundary.behavior: the companion's native status/review/recovery surface is the fallback
native_fallback_boundary.gate_failure_routing: if G-ADDIN fails outright, the PRD-required Outlook add-in capability is blocked and routed to OWN-01 for a product-owner decision
native_fallback_boundary.prohibited: native UI is never a silent substitute for the blocked add-in capability, and no claim advertises add-in support in its place

privacy_boundary.new_persisted_records: none; this ADR introduces no new persisted database record
privacy_boundary.pairing_state_location: any future pairing root remains the already-reserved pairing-root.dpapi blob under ADR-005's DPAPI boundary, owned by ADR-010 with ADR-005 storage constraints
privacy_boundary.session_state_location: session secrets remain memory-only and are never a database record
privacy_boundary.revision_requirement: introducing any future persisted bridge record requires a separate ADR-PRIV-001 revision; this ADR approves none
